ops.title: Linux port: settled safe-default semantics while the consent choice is pending
ops.body:
Decision record for the cookiesync Linux port (branch yasyf/cookiesync-linux, task b97e618). Source: root bus contracts #97 and #101 on bus e46fc748, 2026-09-30.

The owner has been asked one preference by root (approve Linux browser-session access on the Mac via the existing Touch ID route, versus explicit approval inside the VM). Until it is answered, the port implements only the safe existing semantics:

- Linux presence probe returns a successful unattended snapshot: never an error (a probe error is treated as attended by `routesConsent`), never attended. A Linux host is never a consent approver and answers `unavailable`.
- Local presence-gated key release on Linux fails closed and routes to an attended Mac peer through the existing routed-consent path when one is already configured.
- Linux key cache is the existing degraded MEMORY tier with the 5 minute cap; it never claims ENCLAVE.
- No key downgrade: Linux Chromium crypto follows the store's own tag (v10 fixed key, v11 Secret Service key, SHA-256(host_key) prefix only at meta.version >= 24); writes match the store's tag or refuse.
- The VM is a pull-only consumer: no registration as a full Mac mesh peer, no full-shell ssh key provisioning, no pairing automation. Root reviews any proposed pairing.
- Bridge Chrome on Linux: headless without a display, never `--no-sandbox`, no `--password-store` flag.
- Pins: daemonkit v0.32.1, synckit v0.37.0; all work is cookiesync-side, no dependency worktree.

Why recorded: recon showed that a naive Linux presence or consent stub would let a headless VM approve a Mac key release without Touch ID, and that writing v10 into a v11 store silently lowers encryption while the reverse makes Chrome delete the eTLD+1 cookie group.
